audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t both cite a 48.89% win rate; the packet says 55.86% over 324 games.
audit.why: The rendered difficulty text contradicts the win-rate number shown elsewhere on the page.
audit.corrected: Both strings now state 55.86% while keeping the 5/10 difficulty (the lane is genuinely lost early and won late).

audit.why: Four spikes exist and map to Lvl 3-5 / Lvl 6 / 1st item / Late; the level-6 spike text needed the R cooldown and the QSS claim removed, not a re-ordering.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text now carries Realm of Death's 140/120/100 cooldown and the Alpha Strike untargetable answer instead of an unverifiable cleanse claim.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer repeatedly calls Indestructible his E. Indestructible is W (shield/heal); E is Death's Grasp, the pull. whys[3] also called R a pull.
audit.why: Slot labels drive what the player watches for; telling them the shield is on E means they track the wrong cooldown and mis-time their all-in.
audit.corrected: Every 'Indestructible (E)' is now 'Indestructible (W)', and the pull is named Death's Grasp (E) with its 16/14/12/10/8 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named the right ability but carried no numbers.
audit.why: Real cooldowns make the punish window concrete.
audit.corrected: E is 16s at rank 1, Obliterate ramps 8s to 4s, R is 140/120/100.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text asserted 'Quick Silver-style cleanse is your friend' against Realm of Death.
audit.why: Cleanse/QSS eligibility is not in the kit data and I could not verify it; asserting it could send a player into the realm holding a useless item.
audit.corrected: Claim removed and replaced with the verifiable Alpha Strike untargetable window.
sources: kit files carry no cleanse/QSS data

edits.before: At 2 his Q chunk plus Indestructible (E) heal keep every exchange his.
edits.after: At 2 his Q chunk plus Indestructible (W) shield-heal keeps exchanges his.

edits.before: Level 3 his full DoT-and-shield kit out-sustains your early damage.
edits.after: Level 3 his Death's Grasp (E) pull into an isolated Q out-damages you.

edits.before: By 4-5 it's a skill window — dodging his Q and R pull keeps you even.
edits.after: By 4-5 it's a skill window — dodging his Q and E pull keeps you even.

edits.before: Morde chunks you with Obliterate (Q) and his passive Darkness Rise DoT, and Indestructible (E) heals and shields him; farm at Alpha Strike (Q) range and never sit in his Darkness Rise aura or eat a full Q.
edits.after: Morde chunks you with Obliterate (Q) and his Darkness Rise aura, and Indestructible (W) banks that damage as a shield he can eat to heal; farm at Alpha Strike (Q) range and never take an isolated Q, which hits far harder.

edits.before: His Realm of Death (R) rips you into a 1v1 death realm where he steals your stats — if he lands it you likely lose, so keep Alpha Strike (Q) ready and Quick Silver-style cleanse is your friend; do not fight while his R is up.
edits.after: His Realm of Death (R) rips you into a 1v1 where he steals your stats — pre-item you lose that duel, so hold Alpha Strike (Q) to go untargetable through his opening burst; at 140s rank 1 it is down a long time, so fight in that window.

edits.before: You out-scale — true damage ignores his stacked resistances and Highlander (R) resets let you kill through Indestructible (E), but his Realm of Death (R) is still a coinflip 1v1, so only take it with items and buffs ahead.
edits.after: You out-scale — Wuju Style (E) true damage ignores his stacked resistances and Highlander (R) resets let you kill through Indestructible (W), but his Realm of Death (R) is still a real 1v1, so only take it with items ahead.

edits.before: Mordekaiser owns the early lane — Obliterate (Q) chunks, Darkness Rise passive burns you in melee, and Indestructible (E) heals whatever you trade, so hover at Alpha Strike (Q) range, avoid his aura, and only Q in for cannon.
edits.after: Mordekaiser owns the early lane — Obliterate (Q) chunks, Darkness Rise burns you in melee, and Indestructible (W) heals back whatever you trade, so hover at Alpha Strike (Q) range, avoid his aura, and only Q in for cannon.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are a skill window centered on his Realm of Death (R): if you avoid getting pulled into the death realm and bait his Q, Alpha Strike (Q) and Wuju Style (E) true damage keep you even, but eat his full combo and his shield-heal wins.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 hinge on Death's Grasp (E), 16s at rank 1: it is the pull that isolates his Q for bonus damage, so trade only while it is down. Alpha Strike (Q) and Wuju Style (E) true damage keep you even; eat the full combo and his W shield-heal wins.

edits.before: You take over with items — true damage ignores his magic-tank resistances, Alpha Strike (Q) dodges Obliterate (Q), and Highlander (R) resets kill through Indestructible (E); the one caveat is his Realm of Death (R) 1v1, which you only accept when ahead.
edits.after: You take over with items — Wuju Style (E) true damage ignores his magic-tank resistances, Alpha Strike (Q) blinks untargetable through his burst, and Highlander (R) resets kill through Indestructible (W); accept his Realm of Death (R) duel only with items ahead.

edits.before: To sustain trades with Indestructible (E) shield and heal
edits.after: To sustain trades with Indestructible (W) shield and heal

edits.before: Track his E (Death's Grasp pull) — it's his entire engage and isolation setup; when it's down he can't safely force the Q-slam trade. Past 6, track Realm of Death cooldown and never fight when you'd be caught in it without Alpha Strike up.
edits.after: Track Death's Grasp (E) — 16s at rank 1 and his entire isolation setup; when it's down he can't force the Q-slam trade, and Obliterate only ramps from 8s to 4s. Past 6, Realm of Death is 140/120/100 — never fight in that window without Alpha Strike up.

edits.before: It rates a 5/10 because the win rate is dead even (48.89%) — it's a clean scaling race with no unfightable mechanic. He owns five of seven stages but your two-item power is so dominant that the lane equalizes; the difficulty is purely the discipline to not die in the long early window.
edits.after: It rates a 5/10 even though you take it 55.86% — it's a clean scaling race with no unfightable mechanic. He owns five of seven stages but your two-item power is so dominant that the lane more than equalizes; the difficulty is purely the discipline to not die in the long early window.

edits.before: A dead-even scaling race (48.89%) — Morde owns the long early, but Yi's two-item on-hit and Alpha Strike's realm-dodge make the late lane his; pure patience check, 5/10 to play.
edits.after: A scaling race Yi takes 55.86% — Morde owns the long early, but Yi's two-item on-hit and Alpha Strike's realm-dodge make the late lane his; pure patience check, 5/10 to play.

notes: The kit file flags Obliterate (Q) with 'grounding', and _missing suggests Morde can deny Alpha Strike with it. Riot's own Obliterate description says only that it smashes the ground for damage, increased on a single target — no grounding. Per the brief's rule I trusted the description and wrote no grounding claim. Level chart (phases[].side and win[]) already agrees with the packet chart; no chart edits proposed.
